reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement with 'two-fold increase in vaccine specific interferon gamma secretion' demonstrating immune activation. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear pathway modulation evidenced by interferon gamma secretion increase, confirming T-cell activation downstream of antigen presentation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed clinical results - the primary immunologic response endpoint was met (7/31 responses in MART-1 27-35 arm), but clinical response rates were modest (effect size 1) across most arms. Some peptide formulations (26-35 27L) showed no immunologic response. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Different peptide formulations showed varying efficacy - MART-1 27-35 was most effective, while 26-35 27L formulation failed completely. IL-2 combination showed partial benefit but with increased toxicity. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a formulation optimization study comparing different peptide sequences rather than a definitive efficacy trial. The mixed results reflect differential antigen presentation efficiency across peptide variants.

failure_modes.evidence: MART-1 27-35 formulation achieved immunologic responses while 26-35 27L formulation completely failed, indicating mechanism works only with specific peptide sequences
